facts.fact: The article was published on May 13, 2026.
The article is titled "8 Social Media Trends for Small Business in 2026," so it lists eight trends.
facts.quote: 8 Social Media Trends for Small Business in 2026

facts.fact: The article recommends starting AI personalization with three audience groups: existing customers, first-time prospects, and local intent audiences.
facts.quote: Three groups are usually enough to start:

facts.fact: The article states that AI can produce twenty versions of a headline in minutes, but cannot determine which claim a market will believe.
facts.quote: AI can produce twenty versions of a headline in minutes.

facts.fact: The author says small businesses should test about five versions of a short-form video concept rather than spend weeks polishing one.
facts.quote: I see small businesses lose weeks polishing one video when they should have tested five.

facts.fact: The page recommends that small businesses run a repeat creator program with three to five creators, each covering a different angle of trust, rather than relying on one sponsored post.
facts.quote: The best setup for many SMBs is not one sponsored post. It is a repeat creator program with three to five people who each cover a different angle of trust.

facts.fact: Sprout Social states that social platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube drive over 60% of product discovery globally in 2026 projections.
facts.quote: social platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube drive over 60% of product discovery globally in 2026 projections

facts.fact: The Adwave article recommends that small businesses start live streaming with one 15 to 20 minute session each week to test format, timing, and audience questions.
facts.unit: minutes per session, once per week
facts.quote: One 15 to 20 minute session each week is enough to test format, timing, and audience questions.

facts.fact: The article recommends running one demand-capture trend and one trust trend consistently for a quarter before using the results to shape broader marketing.
facts.quote: Run both consistently for a quarter. Track the actions that matter. Then use what performs to shape your broader marketing.
